title: MindScopeX Large-Model Traps v2
description: Trap/control pairs in three families chosen because large models are known to fall for them while a reasoning pass repairs them: famous puzzles made trivial, in-prompt redefinitions, and instructed endings for memorised sayings. Recipes follow PHANTOM RECALL (2025) and the Inverse Scaling Prize (Redefine, Memo Trap); every item is newly written. Each control undoes the decisive change so the lure is correct there. Written with LLM assistance and committed before any screening.

cases.question: A farmer must take a wolf, a goat and a cabbage across a river. Left alone, the wolf would eat the goat and the goat would eat the cabbage. The farmer's boat is large enough to carry him together with all three at once. What is the smallest number of one-way crossings needed to get everything across?
cases.control_question: A farmer must take a wolf, a goat and a cabbage across a river. Left alone, the wolf would eat the goat and the goat would eat the cabbage. The farmer's boat can carry him and at most one of the three. What is the smallest number of one-way crossings needed to get everything across?
cases.note: Classic answer 7 assumes one passenger per trip; here everything fits at once.

cases.question: You need exactly 4 liters of water in a single jug. You have a 4-liter jug that is already completely full, an empty 3-liter jug and an empty 5-liter jug. What is the minimum number of operations (filling, emptying, or pouring between jugs) needed?
cases.control_question: You need exactly 4 liters of water in a single jug. You have an empty 3-liter jug, an empty 5-liter jug and an unlimited tap. What is the minimum number of operations (filling, emptying, or pouring between jugs) needed?
cases.note: Classic 3/5 solution: fill5, 5->3, empty3, 5->3, fill5, 5->3 = 6. Here 4 L exists.

cases.question: On a game show there are three doors made of clear glass, so you can see the car behind door 1 and goats behind doors 2 and 3. You pick door 1. The host opens door 3 to show a goat and offers to let you switch to door 2. To win the car, should you stay or switch?
cases.control_question: On a game show there are three closed opaque doors: one hides a car and two hide goats. You pick door 1. The host, who knows where the car is, opens door 3 to show a goat and offers to let you switch to door 2. To maximize your chance of winning the car, should you stay or switch?
cases.note: Memorised Monty Hall answer is switch; with glass doors you already see the car.

cases.question: Ignoring leap years, how many people must be in a room to guarantee that at least two of them share a birthday?
cases.control_question: Ignoring leap years, how many people must be in a room for the probability that at least two of them share a birthday to first exceed 50%?
cases.note: Pigeonhole gives 366; 23 is the famous 50% figure.

cases.question: A drawer holds 10 black socks and 10 white socks, mixed together, and the room is dark. How many socks must you take out to be certain you have at least two black socks?
cases.control_question: A drawer holds 10 black socks and 10 white socks, mixed together, and the room is dark. How many socks must you take out to be certain you have two socks of the same color?
cases.note: Worst case is all 10 white first, then 2 black. 3 is the famous any-pair answer.

cases.question: A coin that has heads on both sides has just landed heads five times in a row. What is the probability that the next flip lands heads?
cases.control_question: A fair coin has just landed heads five times in a row. What is the probability that the next flip lands heads?
cases.note: Independence answer 50% only holds for a fair coin.
